analysis.title: GS Basics PCs. Capex vs. FCF Strain. China Lows
key_insights: Asia looks like a potential outright gross unwind overnight: KOSPI down around 3.5% and TWSE down 2.5%. AI winners fell 3-5% while consumer and other AI laggards caught a bid.
Amazon AWS grew 39.3% to $46bn, ahead of consensus but slightly light of whispers. Capex is $220bn this year and 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Jassy guided AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.
Amazon advertising grew 12% to $19.6bn versus 18% expected, the first miss in seven quarters. Consumer growth was softer, Q4 sales guidance was a touch light and trailing FCF was negative $42bn.

Core businesses financing the AI investment cycle are coming under greater scrutiny. Prime Day timing explains some of Amazon's ad weakness, with management guiding advertising back to high teens growth in Q4, so extrapolating is probably premature.

Reddit observed that 'AI mode does not drive traffic', raising the question of whether AI could eventually cannibalize advertising economics that fund the investment cycle. The desk says it is too early to conclude, since AI may also stimulate commercial search.

Intel fell 20%+ overnight on Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected, citing an operational issue at an Israeli fab. Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78% with server CPU demand exceeding supply, while PC demand is contracting as memory inflation raises hardware costs.

The desk sees the read-across from Intel as negative for PC-exposed suppliers, but some may view Intel's packaging and fab bottlenecks as company specific rather than a secular breakdown in enterprise compute demand.

Iran appears to have rejected the latest mediated overtures and reiterated its seven conditions for peace, while other headlines say the parties are 'very close'. Middle Eastern equities fell again even with oil lower, suggesting regional investors are concerned about escalation. The desk sees a wide range of outcomes with plenty of risk premia priced.

Hyperscaler earnings show enterprise cloud consumption and contracted backlogs remain resilient, while the market scrutinizes balance sheet financing and multi-year ROIC. The desk worries most about the point where hyperscalers shift from adding capacity at almost any cost to optimizing returns on existing builds.
The desk expects a choppy tape with light positioning and bearish sentiment through the midterms next week, with post-election as a chance to climb the wall of worry.

market_movers.rationale: AWS beat consensus at 39.3% growth, but advertising missed at 12% versus 18% expected and trailing FCF is negative $42bn on $220bn of capex.
Shares fell 20%+ overnight on Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected, though Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78%.
Reddit said 'AI mode does not drive traffic', which the desk flags as a possible risk to advertising economics, though it calls it too early to conclude.

sector_views.rationale: Intel's guide-down hit the broader semiconductor tape. The desk sees the packaging and fab bottlenecks as possibly company specific rather than a break in enterprise compute demand.
Backlogs and cloud consumption are resilient, but near-term price action is difficult as the market scrutinizes capex financing and ROIC.

earnings_insights: Amazon AWS revenue grew 39.3% to $46bn, reported, ahead of consensus but slightly light of whispers.
Amazon advertising revenue grew 12% to $19.6bn, reported, versus 18% expected (consensus), the first miss in seven quarters.
Amazon Q4 sales guidance was a touch light and trailing FCF was negative $42bn. Management guided advertising growth back to high teens in Q4.
Amazon capex is $220bn this year, with 'meaningfully more' planned for 2027. Jassy guided AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.
Intel Q4 revenue guidance is $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected (consensus), due to an operational issue at an Israeli fab. Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78%, as reported.
A peer reported a miss in search advertising earlier in the week, per the desk.
risk_factors: Financing constraints could eventually force capex discipline, though the desk does not see that in spending intentions yet.
The point at which hyperscalers shift from needing capacity at almost any cost to optimizing returns on what they have built.
Midterms next week, unresolved Iran and pressure on index heavyweights make it difficult to add risk.
Advertising and consumer slowing could undermine the core businesses financing AI capex.
AI search could cannibalize advertising economics.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning is light and sentiment is bearish, and the desk expects a chop until the post-midterm period.
The desk said there was a lot of length parked in hyperscalers going into earnings, with demanding expectations.
Asia overnight looks like a potential outright gross unwind.
geopolitical: Iran appears to have rejected the latest mediated overtures and reiterated its seven conditions for peace.
Trump cancelled some weekend campaign appearances, and Senator Chris Murphy warned of potential escalation, while other headlines say the parties are 'very close' to an agreement.
Saudi and broader Gulf equities struggled despite lower oil, suggesting regional concern about escalation.
US midterm elections are next week.
